name: Jungle Ruins
description: Follow an old river road into a jungle-swallowed city of terraces, courtyards, and flooded vaults. Read the water marks left by its builders, find shelter beneath the canopy, and face the stone guardian at the source of the city's lost aqueduct.

items.name: Bronze Machete
items.description: A broad bronze blade sharpened for cutting through vines and close fighting.

items.name: River Spear
items.description: A hardwood spear tipped with a narrow bronze point.

items.name: Woven Shield
items.description: A sturdy reed shield bound around a light wooden frame.

items.name: Barkcloth Vest
items.description: Layers of treated barkcloth with small wooden plates sewn inside.

items.name: Herbal Poultice
items.description: A packet of crushed leaves and clean cloth carried by river travelers.

properties.use_message: You apply the poultice and catch your breath. (The expedition's standard recovery rules apply.)

items.name: Fruit Ration
items.description: Dried fruit wrapped in a broad leaf against the rain.

properties.use_message: The fruit is tart and sustaining. (The expedition's standard recovery rules apply.)

items.name: Resin Torch
items.description: A wrapped torch whose resin burns even in heavy damp.

properties.use_message: The resin catches, lighting the mossy stone and low hanging roots.

items.name: Terrace Token
items.description: A carved stone token marked with the same channels as the lower sluice gate.

items.name: Aqueduct Seal
items.description: A heavy bronze seal shaped to fit the lock beyond the headwater court.

items.name: River Beadwork
items.description: A strand of polished river stones and glass beads found beneath fallen leaves.

items.name: Carved Slate
items.description: A small slate showing the city's water channels before the forest returned.

items.name: Sluice Coffer
items.description: A sealed wooden coffer tucked into a dry recess beside the lower sluice.

items.name: Headwater Casket
items.description: A stone casket carved with winding channels and capped by a bronze lid.

npcs.name: River Guide
npcs.description: A local guide taking shelter beneath a broken arch, with a careful sketch of the terraces on a bark sheet.

nodes.body: 'The old builders led water through every level. Follow the dry channel to the lower sluice, but test the stones before crossing. One dropped away under me.'

responses.text: Where does the channel lead after the sluice?

nodes.body: 'Up to the headwater court. The guardian still stands there, beside the seal for the last gate.'

npcs.name: Ruin Surveyor
npcs.description: A patient surveyor copying water marks from a wall while rain runs off a broad leaf above the notes.

nodes.body: 'These cuts mark flood heights, not dates. The lower court was kept dry with a gate. Its stone token should still be near the old winch.'

responses.text: I will search by the winch.

enemies.name: Root Spider
enemies.description: A large brown spider poised among the roots above a narrow path.

enemies.name: Canopy Monkey
enemies.description: A bold monkey that drops from the branches to defend its gathered food.

enemies.name: River Crocodile
enemies.description: A broad-backed crocodile sliding through the flooded stone channels.

enemies.name: Mossbound Sentinel
enemies.description: A jointed stone watchman covered in moss, still walking its assigned terrace.

enemies.name: Headwater Guardian
enemies.description: A towering stone figure with channels carved down its arms; water runs through them as it rises before the final gate.

descriptions.text: A broken stone gateway rises from the riverbank. Thick roots grip its lintel, and a stepped road disappears beneath the green canopy.
A stair worn smooth by water reaches a quiet bend in the river. Beyond the ruined walls, an open trail follows the bank toward daylight.
A dry channel ends at a jammed stone gate. Beside the old winch, a narrow recess holds a sealed coffer above the high water mark.
Water spills between high terraces into a round basin. A huge carved guardian blocks the bronze-fitted gate behind it, its stone hands wet with spray.
Vines curtain a path between low walls. Their leaves hide cracks in the paving and an older trail of footprints.
Roots have lifted the paving into uneven ridges. Dappled light reveals a line of worn channel markers.
Tall trees shade an open courtyard. Fallen fruit scatters around a dry fountain, while small movements rustle high overhead.
Dark water fills the gallery to the ankles. Reliefs of rivers and hills continue below the waterline, where silt clouds around each step.
Broad steps climb between mossy retaining walls. Small channels once carried rainwater down either side.
Rows of stone counters stand under the trees. Seeds have sprouted in their cracks, and broken weights lie in the leaf litter.
A shallow pool collects rain beneath open sky. Smooth seats ring the water, and one outlet gurgles behind a screen of roots.
From this narrow platform the old river road appears through gaps in the canopy. A toppled stone watcher lies beside its empty plinth.
The passage ends at a corroded winch wrapped in vines. A few carved stone tokens remain caught in its spokes.
A low tunnel follows a narrow watercourse through the hill. Old flood marks rise almost to the ceiling, but the channel is shallow today.
A roofless tower frames a patch of bright sky. Stone sighting lines radiate across its floor, partly buried beneath leaves.
Rain drips from the canopy long after the clouds have passed.
An insect chorus rises and falls, masking sounds from the next terrace.
Cool mist from the old water channels beads on the stone.
Fresh roots have pried loose several paving stones.
The steady sound of falling water carries from higher in the ruins.
Small channel marks cut into the walls point toward the city's headwaters.

config.objective: Defeat the headwater guardian and recover the aqueduct seal.

config.secret: Search beside the jammed winch for the dry recess.

config.hazard: Dark water hides the edge of the channel.

config.secret: Search under the loose paving beside a channel marker.
